profile.reading:
SV2 is one of nine data centers CoreSite operates across Milpitas, San Jose, and Santa Clara that together make up the company's Silicon Valley campus, a group of interconnected buildings totaling more than 1.4 million square feet that CoreSite markets as a single integrated ecosystem rather than as standalone sites. The building sits at 1656 McCarthy Blvd in Milpitas and totals more than 76,000 square feet on its own, according to CoreSite's own site. CoreSite is a data center and interconnection real estate company that has operated in Silicon Valley for years and is now part of American Tower Corporation, a large publicly traded communications infrastructure company, giving SV2 the backing of one of the country's largest owners of telecommunications real estate.

CoreSite states that SV2 offers both AC and DC power options, backed by 2N UPS redundant power and diverse utility feeds, and the company backs the facility with a 100 percent uptime service level agreement, a guarantee typically reserved for buildings with mature, well-tested redundant infrastructure. Customers can deploy in full cabinets, private cages, or private suites, though CoreSite notes it does not offer partial cabinet configurations at this site. On connectivity, the company advertises access to more than 115 networks across the broader campus, a direct on-ramp to AWS, its own Open Cloud Exchange platform for multi-cloud connectivity, and participation in three peering exchanges, Any2Exchange, AMS-IX Bay Area, and SFMIX, along with blended internet service ranging from 10 megabits to 10 gigabits per second. Security and compliance certifications listed for the site include SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, supported by biometric scanners, key card access, mantrap entries, a perimeter fence, and round the clock video surveillance and remote hands staffing.

What CoreSite does not publish for SV2 specifically is the year the building was constructed, a technical or raised-floor square footage figure distinct from the overall building size, a specific IT power capacity in megawatts, or a current tenant list, information the company treats as confidential given the competitive, high-density nature of the Silicon Valley colocation market where its customers include many of the region's largest technology and networking companies.
profile.research_note: Operator states "76,000+" sqft (written as 76000, actual may be slightly higher); 2N UPS redundancy; 100% uptime SLA. No technical/raised-floor sqft, IT capacity MW, year built, or generator MW published.

profile.research_note: CoreSite Real Estate 1656 McCarthy, L.P. (and the related 1656 McCarthy GP, L.L.C.) is a California property-holding legal entity for CoreSite's Silicon Valley campus building at 1656 McCarthy Boulevard, Milpitas, California, confirmed via California business entity records. CoreSite structures individual campus properties under separate LP/LLC legal entities, a standard REIT practice; this is the same underlying operating company as the main CoreSite record in this registry (uid 2bf5e117), a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation. Retained as a separate row per this registry's no-deletion policy and cross-linked via duplicate_of.

reading.body:
CoreSite Real Estate 1656 McCarthy, L.P. is a single purpose property holding entity, not an operating company, and the registry row exists because REITs title each building under its own limited partnership.

The entity name is an address, and the address is a real building. CoreSite SV2 stands at 1656 McCarthy Boulevard in Milpitas, California, published at more than 76,000 square feet, one of nine CoreSite facilities the company describes as a Silicon Valley campus of more than 1.4 million square feet. CoreSite's 2020 annual report lists this entity and its general partner alongside roughly forty similarly named subsidiaries, each paired with a general partner company, which is ordinary REIT practice for financing, liability and tax reasons. A registry seeded from ownership records will therefore produce one apparent operator per building.

For AI specifically, the useful fact is what CoreSite chooses to publish about SV2 and what it does not. It publishes interconnection: more than 115 campus networks, an on site Amazon Web Services on ramp, the Any2Exchange, AMS-IX Bay Area and SFMIX peering fabrics, and a common language location identifier of MLPSCASD. It publishes no critical IT load, no utility service size and no generator rating. The building is marketed on connectivity rather than density, and the power figures that would let a reader judge its capacity to host compute are absent.

The ownership chain is documented. American Tower Corporation acquired CoreSite Realty Corporation in late 2021, and its annual report for 2025 states 30 operating data centre facilities across eleven United States markets at 31 December 2025, with data centre segment revenue of 1,053.1 million dollars for the year. Investment vehicles affiliated with Stonepeak Partners LP hold mandatorily convertible preferred equity in the United States data centre business.

What this data does not cover is the physical constraint that matters most. There is no megawatt figure, no utility service size, no generator rating and no construction year for SV2, so nothing here indicates how much compute the building can support or how close it sits to a power limit. The campus square footage describes floor area, not electrical capacity, and the two should not be read as interchangeable.
